generatedCommentsNodes.comment: In the "index param - root arrays" test, the expected output for `obj_default.trace` changes from a single flattened array `trace.id: [aa, bb]` to two indexed entries `trace.0.id: bb` and `trace.1.id: aa`. The element order is reversed relative to the old expectation. If the indexed document contains `trace: [{id: "aa"}, {id: "bb"}]`, the synthetic source should preserve that order (`trace.0.id: aa`, `trace.1.id: bb`). The reversal suggests that, without the second parsing pass, array elements may be captured in reverse document order. Please confirm this is the intended and correct ordering, since array element order is semantically significant for consumers of the synthetic source.

review_comment: Not sure if it's safe to remove a setting, would this cause issues with rolling upgrades? It shouldn't be set anywhere, of course.

Shard of indices using setting would not be able allocate if this setting is used, but it has been removed. That what branches did this setting get back ported? I think just removing the setting, should fix the issue, but would be good to double check this.
This was added to 8.16, not used anywhere as it's a last-resort setting: https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/114649
I see. I'm not against removing this. I was trying to quantify the severity of the issue if someone ends up using this setting and then upgrades.
